requirements_slice.system_goal: Make the current backend active slice formally addressable through strict-GRACE module contracts, module maps, function contracts, and semantic START/END blocks before deeper backend refactor and maximal observability work.

in_scope.item: Add and align module contracts, module maps, function contracts, and semantic START/END blocks for backend/app/main.py, backend/app/logging_utils.py, backend/app/middleware/correlation.py, backend/app/services/day_brief.py, backend/app/services/day_brief_validators.py, backend/app/services/week_brief_service.py, backend/app/services/scheduler.py, and backend/app/services/analytics.py.
Use existing well-marked backend modules as the local strict-GRACE style reference.
Make backend post-test evidence for Day, Week, report readout, scheduler, analytics, and correlation/logging glue readable by stable module/function/block names.
Separate W01 packet-local read-only evidence ownership from W02 wave-final canonical today-week observability ownership.

out_of_scope.item: Day or Week business semantic changes.
Maximal logging rewrite or observability redesign.
Deep refactor or split of backend/app/services/report_workflow.py.

use_case.summary: Prepare the current backend active slice for strict-GRACE packet execution and observability follow-on work by making module boundaries and runtime evidence formally addressable.
use_case.scenario: Each touched active-slice module exposes an explicit module contract and module map aligned to the local repository style.
Exported, orchestration, and side-effect entrypoints in the touched modules have function contracts where the local strict-GRACE style requires them.
W01 implementation packets can be evaluated with packet-local backend evidence and read-only post-test review without claiming canonical today-week closeout.
W02 final post-test evidence for the touched Day, Week, report-read, scheduler, analytics, and correlation/logging paths is readable by module/function/block names without guesswork.

business_invariants.invariant: Canon-sync edits may tighten GRACE addressability but must not change payload semantics for DayBrief, WeekBrief, report read endpoints, scheduler jobs, or analytics writes.
Correlation, module, function, and block naming must become more explicit without forcing a new logging transport or a full middleware architecture rewrite.
Packet-local implementation evidence and wave-final canonical observability are separate lanes and must not be conflated.

expected_failure_handling.item: If a target file cannot be aligned to local strict-GRACE style without semantic risk, keep business behavior unchanged and record the remaining gap explicitly for follow-on refactor work.
If W01 packet-local verification passes but evidence lacks readable module/function/block attribution, implementation remains incomplete until the gap is corrected or explicitly documented.
If W02 canonical today-week evidence is absent, fragmented, or unexpectedly degraded, the wave blocks architect acceptance.

success_criteria.criterion: The bounded active-slice files expose stable module contracts, module maps, and semantic block boundaries consistent with the existing local strict-GRACE style.
Function contracts are added only where the active slice exports or orchestrates externally meaningful work; no untouched clean modules are rewritten just for consistency theater.

W01 packet-local backend quick, targeted pytest, and read-only post-test review evidence can be attributed to the touched active-slice files by stable module/function/block naming without claiming final canonical observability.
W02 final verifier evidence owns canonical today-week observability and records a clean, degraded-but-expected, unexpected-degradation, or no-evidence-blocker verdict before architect acceptance.
